clue.text: The only place to pack, as a precaution?

definitions.meaning: read playfully: 'only' is JUST and the place where things are packed is IN a CASE
describes doing something to be safe should a need arise

explanation.surface: Travel advice: pack everything into one bag, to be on the safe side.
explanation.walkthrough: The first stretch is split as JUST (only) plus IN CASE (the place where things get packed).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the everyday idiom for doing something as a safeguard against a possible event.

clue.text: Those taking part should be prepared for this rally

definitions.text: Those taking part should be prepared for this rally

parts.words: Those taking part should be prepared for this rally
parts.note: the Scout motto is Be Prepared, and a big international gathering of Scouts has its own special name

explanation.surface: Advice to people joining a protest rally: come prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: The rally looks political, but 'be prepared' is the Scout motto, pointing to a Scouts' gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A large rally of Scouts, national or international, is called by this name.

clue.text: Welcome Sarah, leading North American

indicators.note: Sarah's short form goes at the front, ahead of the second piece

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah
the Ute are a Native American people of Utah and Colorado

explanation.surface: Greeting Sarah, who is heading up a North American group.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone with a gesture of respect, such as a raised hand, is a form of welcoming them.

clue.text: Not beaten by the clock early enough

definitions.meaning: finishing before a deadline runs out
arriving or happening with no lateness, punctually

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same idea: beating a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both before the deadline expires and not late, punctual for an appointment.

clue.text: Magazine with chapter on painting band

indicators.note: in a down clue, the chapter letter sits on top of the rest

parts.note: painting is a form of art
a ridge is a long narrow strip or band, as in a ridge of high pressure

explanation.surface: A magazine article with a chapter about a painting band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' suggests a periodical, but it is the part of a gun that holds ammunition, or a holder for film or ink.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in a firearm or camera is a container loaded into it, as is the cylinder holding a round.

clue.text: Apology for a dance

definitions.meaning: a polite phrase said when bumping into someone or interrupting
a ballroom dance in which a dancer may cut in and take another's partner

explanation.surface: Someone apologising for asking a partner onto the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite pardon phrase also names an old ballroom dance where partners can be claimed by others.

clue.text: Burn coming from ocean before river

indicators.note: the ocean piece comes ahead of the river letter

parts.note: an ocean is a sea
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A burn that comes from the ocean before reaching a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' can be a Scottish stream, fitting the water imagery, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch the surface of something with strong heat is to burn it.

clue.text: Short view over a city in outline of plot

indicators.note: in a down clue, the trimmed view sits over the rest
being short, the word for a view loses its final letter

parts.note: a scene is a view or vista
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A brief view looking over a city, as in a map's outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay synopsis setting out the sequence of events is a sketch of how a story will unfold.

clue.text: Article babu hid travelling in capital

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about an Indian clerk, a babu, who hid while travelling in a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges BABU HID into BUDHABI; a babu is an Indian clerk or gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: I landed amongst new army — the army!

indicators.note: the I and the word for landed sit among the rearranged army letters
new signals the army letters made into a fresh order

parts.note: lit means landed, as a bird lit on a branch

explanation.surface: A soldier boasting of landing among a fresh army.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter reuses 'army' as both fodder and definition; the exclamation mark flags the playful repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces as a body, as in 'the military were called in', are the soldiers collectively.

clue.text: Stop said form of payment

indicators.note: said tells us the word for stop is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to check is to halt or stop

explanation.surface: A spoken instruction to cancel a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A written order to a bank to pay money is a familiar, if old-fashioned, way to pay.

clue.text: Be too clever with old-fashioned vehicles making a comeback

parts.note: out means out of fashion

indicators.note: coming back means the vehicles word is read backwards

parts.note: trams are vehicles running on rails

explanation.surface: Getting too clever by bringing back vintage vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone by cunning is to beat them in wits.

clue.text: Was twisting the bandage

indicators.note: the letters of was are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was twisting a bandage while applying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bandage' is a verb here, to wrap up, not the noun it first seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something up in strips of cloth is to bind it, as with a dressing.

clue.text: Short measure

definitions.meaning: a short is a small drink of spirits such as whisky
an old unit of weight, one sixteenth of an ounce

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like one phrase meaning a stingy pour, but splits into a drink and a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tot of whisky has this name, and it is also an avoirdupois unit of weight.

clue.text: Personality only seen or heard at intervals

definitions.text: Personality only seen or heard at intervals

parts.words: Personality only seen or heard at intervals
parts.note: a broadcaster who introduces programmes appears in the breaks between them

explanation.surface: A celebrity who pops up only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' suggests rarity, but means the gaps between broadcast programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter on radio or TV who introduces programmes is heard or seen between shows.

clue.text: Avoidance of notice that's given out outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the notice word
out signals the letters of given are scattered into a new order

parts.note: an ad is a notice, short for advertisement

explanation.surface: Ignoring a notice that has been handed out outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GIVEN into EVING, which goes 'outside' AD. 'Avoidance' is a noun, and the answer works as a verbal noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging or escaping something is the act of getting out of it.

clue.text: Charlie, at ten, found in vehicle, getting time off

indicators.note: the middle pieces are found inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
Charlie is C in the phonetic alphabet
IO looks like the figure 10

explanation.surface: Charlie, sitting in a van at ten, setting off on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday or break from work or study is a period when one is not working.

clue.text: One separated from men about to enter dodgy club on base

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the base letter
the men and the about letter go into the dodgy club word

parts.note: a dive is a seedy nightclub or bar
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
c is circa, about
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Someone leaving their partner, after men show up at a seedy club.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose marriage has been legally dissolved is no longer with their spouse.

clue.text: Hen and rat running wild round extreme characters in pilgrimage centre

indicators.note: the rearranged animal letters go round the extreme characters
the hen and rat letters are running wild, scrambled into a new order

parts.note: A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Farm animals running loose around a holy town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link here; 'running wild' acts on the two animal words alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The town in Galilee where Jesus grew up draws Christian pilgrims.

clue.text: Relatively favourable tip once dubious

indicators.note: dubious means doubtful, so the letters are put in a questionable new order

explanation.surface: A betting tip once thought fairly good, now dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing favouritism to family members, especially in giving jobs, is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Muse Clio playing stadium

indicators.note: the letters are at play, moving into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Clio, the Muse of history, performing at a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Roman amphitheatre gives its name to large arenas and theatres.

clue.text: Adult having energy; about time!

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult
E is the physics symbol for energy
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: An exasperated adult, full of energy, saying 'about time!'
explanation.definitionFit: An immeasurably long period is an age, a vast stretch of years.

clue.text: Six shot approaching Chaldean city in force

indicators.note: the first pieces come up just before the city name

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a go is a shot or attempt
Ur was an ancient city of Chaldea in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Six shots fired near an ancient city in an armed force.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy and vitality, physical strength, is a sense of force.

clue.text: Expedition in South Africa, some distance inland initially

parts.note: far means at some distance

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of inland

explanation.surface: A trek in South Africa heading some way inland.
explanation.definitionFit: An overland journey, especially to see wild animals in Africa, is this kind of trip.

clue.text: Second prophet with a snack

parts.note: Amos is a Hebrew prophet with a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A second prophet sharing a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried triangular pastry with a spiced filling, from South Asia, is a popular light bite.

clue.text: Dish from southern United Kingdom and two from Rome embracing Asian beast

indicators.note: the Roman two holds the beast inside it

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
the yak is a long-haired ox of Tibet

explanation.surface: A dish from the south of Britain, with two Romans hugging a yak.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese meal of thinly sliced beef cooked with vegetables in a pan at the table.

clue.text: The never-ending round

parts.note: a ring shape has no start and no end, going round forever

explanation.surface: A wearying daily grind that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' suggests routine; it is the shape itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed curved line with no ends is the perfect round figure.

clue.text: Honour a pass received by apprentice falling short

indicators.note: the pass word is taken into the trimmed apprentice word
the apprentice word falls short by dropping its last letter

parts.note: a cadet is a trainee, as in a police cadet
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: An award for a pass mark won by a trainee who nearly failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like an exam result, but it is a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: An award or expression of praise is a mark of esteem.

clue.text: Joint having a cap

parts.note: the patella, a bone covering the front of a leg joint, has a familiar name ending in cap

explanation.surface: A pipe joint fitted with a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg joint between thigh and shin is protected by the patella, which is named after it.

clue.text: It's a shocking thing to be screened

definitions.text: It's a shocking thing to be screened

parts.words: It's a shocking thing to be screened
parts.note: screened means shown in a cinema, and shocking means frightening the audience

explanation.surface: Someone appalled at being medically screened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screened' suggests a medical test; it means shown on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A scary movie, designed to frighten its viewers, is the genre meant.
